title: Closed-immersion right adjoint before restriction
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a
closed immersion, with open
complement $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, and let $A$ be a finite ring.
On the small etale sites, the
direct image $i_*$ has a right
adjoint $Ri^!$ on the
ordinary derived categories.
The functor $i^*$ below is the
inverse image.

proof.text: First extend the closed-support equivalence of [lem-kun-04ca] from abelian sheaves to sheaves of left $A$-modules. An $A_T$-module structure on an abelian sheaf is the compatible action of the constant scalars $a\in A$, extended to the constant ring sheaf by sheafification ([def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]). Explicitly, a section $b$ of $A_T$ is locally represented by constants $a_\lambda$; for a section $s$ of the abelian sheaf, glue $a_\lambda s|_{V_\lambda}$ to define $bs$. Equality of representatives is local, so the glued section is independent of representatives; the module axioms and compatibility with restriction hold locally and hence globally. For a sheaf $M$ of $A_Z$-modules, define the action of a constant $a$ on $(i_*M)(V)=M(V\times_T Z)$ by its action on this last module, then extend it by this gluing construction. This equips the abelian direct image of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] with its module structure for arbitrary $A$, without invoking that definition's commutative-coefficient derived clause. For a supported sheaf $F\cong i_*M$, full faithfulness transports each scalar endomorphism of $F$ uniquely to an endomorphism of $M$. Faithfulness transports the addition, multiplication and identity relations, so these endomorphisms define an $A_Z$-module structure. The same full faithfulness shows that a map is $A$-linear if and only if its transported map is $A$-linear. Thus $i_*$ is fully faithful on module sheaves, its essential image is exactly the module sheaves with zero geometric stalks off $Z$, and $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$; on this essential image $i^*$ is its inverse. No commutativity of $A$ is used.

proof.text: The closed direct image is exact. At a geometric point of $Z$, its stalk is the original stalk, naturally in the sheaf, by [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar]; off $Z$ it is zero by Step 1. Apply this to a short exact sequence of module sheaves on $Z$. Geometric stalks are exact on the underlying abelian sheaves by [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], so the pushed-forward sequence is exact at every stalk. The cohomology sheaves of this three-term sequence have zero stalks: stalks commute with kernels and cokernels, and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] applied to $0\to H$ shows each such sheaf $H$ is zero. Exactness of module sheaves is detected on underlying abelian sheaves, since kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified cokernels ([def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]). Consequently termwise $i_*$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and defines $i_*:D(\mathrm{Mod}(A_Z))\to D(\mathrm{Mod}(A_T))$ by localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. It also computes its own right derived functor: applying $i_*$ to any resolution quasi-isomorphism still gives a quasi-isomorphism.

For an $A_T$-module sheaf $N$, form the kernel $\Gamma_ZN=\ker(N\to j_*j^*N)$ of the inverse/direct-image unit ([def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]). The open immersion $j$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. By both clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], its inverse image is restriction and the unit is the restriction map; these natural identifications respect the scalar maps and hence hold for $A$-modules. Thus, for $V\to T$ etale, $\Gamma_ZN(V)=\ker(N(V)\to N(V\times_TU))$. On any object over $U$ this is the kernel of the identity, so $\Gamma_ZN$ restricts to zero on $U$ and has zero stalks there. Step 1 therefore gives a natural isomorphism $i_*i^*\Gamma_ZN\cong\Gamma_ZN$. For a module sheaf $M$ on $Z$, every map $f:i_*M\to N$ has zero composite to $j_*j^*N$: on $V\times_TU$ its source is $M((V\times_TU)\times_TZ)=M(\varnothing)=0$, since $U$ and $Z$ are complementary. The kernel universal property factors $f$ uniquely through $\Gamma_ZN$. Full faithfulness in Step 1 now gives natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*M,\Gamma_ZN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(M,i^*\Gamma_ZN).$$
Hence the additive functor $i^!_0N:=i^*\Gamma_ZN$ is right adjoint to the exact sheaf functor $i_*$.

proof.text: Use the small site skeleton and universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For either $S=T$ or $S=Z$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] to the constant sheaf of rings $A_S$: its category of left modules is Grothendieck abelian, without requiring $A$ commutative. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence] every complex admits a functorial quasi-isomorphism $K\to I(K)$ to a K-injective complex. The additive functor $i^!_0$ applied termwise gives a functor on homotopy categories: it preserves the equations defining chain maps and homotopies. It commutes with shifts and with the cone formula $C(f)^r=L^r\oplus K^{r+1}$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], because it is additive. Therefore $F:=Q_Z\circ K(i^!_0):K(\mathrm{Mod}(A_T))\to D(\mathrm{Mod}(A_Z))$ is an exact functor of triangulated categories. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to $F$ constructs a functor $Ri^!$ on the entire unbounded derived category, computed by $Ri^!K=Q_Z(i^!_0I(K))$. This also supplies its functoriality and independence of the chosen K-injective replacement.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] to $u=i^!_0$ and $v=i_*$. Step 3 supplies the additive adjunction $v\dashv u$, and Step 2 supplies exactness of $v$. Thus if $I$ is K-injective on $T$, then the termwise complex $i^!_0I$ is K-injective on $Z$. In particular this holds for every $I(K)$ chosen in Step 4; it does not require boundedness or a cohomological-dimension estimate.

Let $M$ be any complex of $A_Z$-modules and $K$ any object of $D(\mathrm{Mod}(A_T))$, with $K\cong Q_TI$ for a K-injective replacement as in Step 4. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] first to $I$, then to the K-injective $i^!_0I$ of Step 5. Between these two applications use the homotopy-category adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] for the additive sheaf adjunction of Step 3. This gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_T)}(i_*Q_ZM,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A_T)}(i_*M,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A_Z)}(M,i^!_0I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_Z)}(Q_ZM,Ri^!K).$$
Here $K(A_S)$ and $D(A_S)$ abbreviate the homotopy and derived categories of $A_S$-module sheaves. Every arrow is natural for chain maps. Since $i_*$ is exact, the two outer expressions invert quasi-isomorphisms in $M$, so this naturality passes through the localization to all derived morphisms in the first variable. In the second variable, morphisms between K-injective representatives are the unique homotopy classes supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; the middle adjunction is natural for these, and Step 4 computes $Ri^!$ on them. Thus the displayed bijection is natural in both derived objects and exhibits $i_*\dashv Ri^!$. All complexes were arbitrary; no constructibility condition or boundedness was introduced.
